name: Science & Technology
description: Physics, biology, space and IT fundamentals for exams.

questions.question: DNA stands for what?
questions.explanation: DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) carries genetic instructions; its double-helix structure was described by Watson and Crick in 1953.

questions.question: Which cell organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate ATP through cellular respiration — hence the powerhouse nickname.

questions.question: Deficiency of Vitamin C causes which disease?
questions.explanation: Scurvy (bleeding gums, fatigue) results from Vitamin C deficiency; rickets from Vitamin D, beriberi from B1, pellagra from B3.

questions.question: Who discovered the ABO blood groups?
questions.explanation: Karl Landsteiner identified the A, B and O blood groups in 1901, winning the Nobel Prize in 1930.

questions.question: Which blood group is called the 'universal donor'?
questions.explanation: O negative blood lacks A, B and Rh antigens, so it can be given to any recipient; AB positive is the universal recipient.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 299,792,458 m/s (~3 × 10⁸ m/s) — the universe's speed limit.

questions.question: Newton's first law of motion is also known as the law of what?
questions.explanation: The first law states that a body remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted on by a force — the principle of inertia.

questions.question: A solution with a pH of 7 is what?
questions.explanation: pH 7 is neutral (pure water); below 7 is acidic, above 7 is basic/alkaline.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of common salt?
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride (NaCl); NaHCO₃ is baking soda and CaCO₃ is limestone/calcium carbonate.

questions.question: A 'light year' is a unit of what?
questions.explanation: A light year is the distance light travels in one year — about 9.46 trillion kilometres.

questions.question: The ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation, lies in which atmospheric layer?
questions.explanation: Ozone is concentrated in the stratosphere (~15–35 km); ozone-depleting CFCs are controlled under the Montreal Protocol.

questions.question: ISRO was founded in 1969 under the leadership of whom?
questions.explanation: Vikram Sarabhai founded ISRO in 1969; Satish Dhawan later chaired it, and A. P. J. Abdul Kalam directed SLV-3.

questions.question: India's first satellite, Aryabhata, was launched in 1975 by which country's rocket?
questions.explanation: Aryabhata (19 April 1975) was launched on a Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket from Kapustin Yar, beginning India's space age.

questions.question: What was the name given to the Chandrayaan-3 landing site near the lunar south pole?
questions.explanation: The Chandrayaan-3 landing site (23 August 2023) was named Shiv Shakti Point; Tiranga Point marks the impact site of Chandrayaan-2.

questions.question: ISRO's Aditya-L1 mission, launched in September 2023, is designed to study what?
options: The Sun, from the L1 Lagrange point
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 observes the Sun from a halo orbit at L1 (~1.5 million km from Earth) — India's first solar observatory mission.

questions.question: The four astronaut-designates of the Gaganyaan mission were selected from which service?
questions.explanation: All four Gaganyaan candidates (incl. Shubhanshu Shukla and Prasanth Nair) are IAF test pilots, trained in India and Russia.

questions.question: What is the basic unit of information in a quantum computer?
questions.explanation: A qubit can exist in superposition of 0 and 1 simultaneously, giving quantum computers their exponential power for certain problems.

questions.question: Commercial 5G services were launched in India in which month and year?
questions.explanation: 5G was rolled out on 1 October 2022; India then became one of the fastest 5G network deployments worldwide.

questions.question: What was the name of India's first nuclear research reactor (1956)?
questions.explanation: Apsara, commissioned in 1956 at BARC (then AEET), was India's — and Asia's — first nuclear research reactor.

questions.question: X-rays were discovered by whom?
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays in 1895, winning the first Nobel Prize in Physics (1901).
